_comment: Signature DATA the watchdog classifies against (spec Section 2 taxonomy + Section 9.3). This is the part that rots at the speed new loop classes appear (6 signatures in May -> F1-F13 in June -> ~19 classes in July), so it is updated ONLY through the repo + sanctioned rollout - never hand-edited on a box. NO secret values live here; the anthropic-family entries are DENY DATA, and secret detection is delegated to scan-no-secrets.sh by version pin.

loop_families.A: AGENT-TURN LOOPS (a model call inside the loop - the token burners)
loop_families.B: PROCESS / SUPERVISOR LOOPS (restart storms; churn + outage, no model call)
loop_families.D: TASK / PROGRESS LOOPS (stalls that look healthy)

loop_classes.name: semantic retry loop / reworded-intent hunt against a fail-closed dependency

tool_loop_block.note: The D5 ignition signature is STRUCTURAL, never prose. The OpenClaw runtime's own identical-call guard emits a session record {type:message, message:{role:toolResult, isError:true, toolName:<tool>, details:{status:'blocked', deniedReason:'tool-loop', reason:<text>}}}. D5 matches on the two ENUM fields above and never on `reason` - so it is language-independent, wording-drift-proof, and carries no message content into a finding. The blocked tool NAME is recorded (counts only); its arguments and the reason prose never are. Confirmed by structural parse of one archived operator-box incident transcript: 1,135 such records, blocked tool names {read, tool_call} - so D5 must NOT hard-code a single tool name.

checkpoint_carrier.note: SECOND CARRIER. Compaction checkpoint summaries can capture the loop transcript VERBATIM; they are re-injected on resume and SURVIVE a session-file roll, so archiving the transcript alone does not clear the poison. Measured: 7 of 16 checkpoint summaries carried the block signature (163 hits) in the incident file vs 0 of 14 in a larger healthy control archive. Detecting this carrier requires a text count over the summary field, so the block sentence is pinned as DATA here rather than compiled into code.

tool_loop_block.checkpoint_text_marker: Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops
tool_loop_block.flush_run_note: The runtime-event prompt that opens a memory-flush run. Measured 9 occurrences (role=user) in the incident transcript, matching the observed burst count - a flush run is the usual ignition context. Recorded as CONTEXT data only; D5 does not require it to fire, because the structural block signature above is sufficient and higher-precision.

fail_closed_markers.match: v0.6.4 TWO-LAYER: a call is fail-closed only when (L1) its tool is NOT in result_scan_exempt_tools AND (L2) the RESULT payload carries a case-insensitive marker substring AND the result ALSO failed at the tool layer OR matches one of error_shape_patterns. Markers alone are no longer sufficient - that was the false-positive engine.
fail_closed_markers.note: The D6 fail-closed signature is pinned as DATA here, exactly like the D5 checkpoint_text_marker, because detecting it requires a text COUNT over the tool-result payload rather than a structural enum match. ONLY THE COUNT ever reaches a finding - the matched text, the surrounding payload, the tool arguments, and any value are never stored, printed, or reproduced. This is the face that catches the incident class the structural signatures cannot: a tool call that SUCCEEDS while the dependency behind it refuses. `exec` running a curl against a fail-closed API exits 0 and is recorded status=completed, so details.status/isError are both clean and every error-keyed detector stays silent. Retrying an auth-class refusal cannot succeed by rewording the request, which is what makes >2 attempts a loop rather than persistence. v0.6.4 ADDS THE SECOND HALF OF THAT SENTENCE: a marker in a result proves only that the WORD is present, never that THIS call was refused. An agent reading a document that discusses authorization was being scored as auth-refused - benign `ls`/`find`/`cat` over one playbook directory holding 5 marker-bearing files produced real escalations on a live box. Marker DENSITY is not the discriminator either: a healthy box measured 7.4% density with 0 spills, equal to or higher than the storm boxes. What separates the two is not how often the word appears but whether the result is shaped like an ERROR at all - hence result_scan_exempt_tools + error_shape_patterns below.
fail_closed_markers.result_scan_exempt_tools_note: L1. These tools' RESULT IS RETRIEVED CONTENT BY CONSTRUCTION - a file's bytes, a stored memory, a tool catalog entry - so a marker in the payload is a property of the DOCUMENT, never of this call's own outcome. They are exempt ONLY from marker scanning; they still count fully toward `calls` and `errors`, so D6 burst detection over read tools is completely preserved. THESE IDS WERE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: a read-only pass over 400 live session transcripts on the operator box, reusing the watchdog's own _tool_result_of and printing DISTINCT tool NAME + COUNT only (never payload text), yielded 14 ids - exec 1401, tool_call 678, tool_search 213, process 127, read 62, message 56, tool_describe 32, cron 13, memory_search 11, write 9, codewhale__deepseek 5, web_fetch 4, sessions_yield 3, web_search 1. The repo's own tool_loop_block note independently records {read, tool_call} from an archived incident transcript. EXTEND THIS LIST ONLY BY THE SAME MEASUREMENT, never by guessing an id that sounds plausible - an id that is not real is dead config, and an id exempted by mistake is a detector that has been silently switched off. DELIBERATELY NOT EXEMPT: `exec` (a shell `cat` of a document is indistinguishable BY TOOL NAME from a curl against a refusing API - that case is carried by L2 instead), and `web_fetch`/`web_search` (a 401 from a fetch is a GENUINE fail-closed dependency and must keep firing).
fail_closed_markers.error_shape_note: L2, and this is the layer that carries the shell-tool case L1 cannot exempt. A marker counts as a refusal only when the result ALSO failed at the tool layer (isError / details.status) or carries one of these STRUCTURAL error shapes: a JSON error key, an HTTP 4xx status line, a JSON status field, or a known CLI failure prefix. Prose cannot produce any of them - a playbook sentence has no quoted-and-colonned JSON key and no status line. Compiled case-insensitive + MULTILINE, once per distinct pattern set; a pattern that fails to compile is skipped rather than killing the tick, because a config typo must never take the watchdog down. A PROSE-PROXIMITY WINDOW (marker within N characters of the word 'error') WAS BUILT, MEASURED AND REJECTED: real playbook prose contains sentences like 'common error: unauthorized access', so the window fails the healthy-box control. Do not reintroduce it. KNOWN RESIDUAL, documented rather than hidden: an `exec` that cats a file containing a VERBATIM structured error dump still scores fail-closed, since by tool name and result shape it is identical to a real refusal. It needs 3+ such reads inside 60s to reach the threshold, and L1 removes the case entirely for native read tools.
fail_closed_markers.deliberately_excluded_note: Bare HTTP status numbers are NOT markers, and are still not markers in v0.6.4. Measured on the operator box's real 998-transcript corpus: including them raises the >=3-in-window pair count from 13 to 37 (2.8x) because '401'/'403' collide with ordinary numeric output - line numbers, byte counts, ports, hashes. The narrow word-shaped marker set is the shippable one; the broad set is recorded here only so a future contributor does not 'improve' the detector by adding them back. NO CONTRADICTION WITH error_shape_patterns ABOVE: 401/403/407 appear there ONLY anchored - inside an HTTP status line (`HTTP/1.1 403`) or as the value of a quoted JSON status field (`"code": 401`). Those are structural positions a byte count or a line number cannot occupy. What stays banned is the BARE numeric substring anywhere in free text, which is what produced the 2.8x inflation.

secret_shapes.note: The secret-CLASS detector is reused verbatim. This pin records which classes the watchdog expects; a class version bump rides the repo, never a box-local edit. The VALUE is never stored, printed, or reproduced.

anthropic_family_deny_note: The watchdog makes ZERO model calls, so this rule is satisfied vacuously at runtime AND enforced statically over every shipped file by guard-no-anthropic-runtime.py. These are deny-list prefixes, never runtime ids; client skills never use Anthropic models.

paid_tier_markers.note: D2 treats a model/provider carrying one of these markers in an idle window as paid-idle burn. A :cloud suffix on a heartbeat model is the classic idle-burn furnace (LP-A2).

process_manager_fields.note: pm2 jlist is filtered to name/status/pid/restarts ONLY, NEVER an env dump - a fleet review leaked live credential VALUES exactly that way, and the standing rule forbids it (spec Section 3, D1).
